solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: African city finally investing in Asian country

indicators.note: something investing a place enters it, so the letter goes inside the country's name

parts.note: Laos is a country in South-East Asia

indicators.note: finally points to the last letter of the word investing

explanation.surface: A traveller's African city at last puts its money into an Asian nation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'investing' does double duty in the surface but its last letter G is what goes inside LAOS, signalled by 'investing in'.
explanation.definitionFit: Lagos is Nigeria's largest city, on the West African coast.

clue.text: One sends up pilots on manoeuvres involving America

indicators.note: involving means taking in, so the abbreviation goes inside the rearranged letters
letters on manoeuvres are moved about, so the letters of pilots and on are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone scrambles aircrew in exercises involving the United States.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sends up' sounds like launching aircraft but means mocks. 'on manoeuvres' looks like one phrase; 'on' is fodder and 'manoeuvres' alone rearranges PILOTSON into LPOONIST, then 'involving' takes AM inside.
explanation.definitionFit: To send up is to mock or satirise, which is what a writer of satirical attacks does.

clue.text: Leaders of group using Telemann's material for strings

indicators.note: the leaders of words are their opening letters, taken here from three words in a row

explanation.surface: A baroque ensemble plays Telemann's music on stringed instruments.
explanation.walkthrough: Telemann, a German baroque composer, fits the musical surface; only his initial counts.
explanation.definitionFit: Catgut, gut for short, is the traditional animal-intestine cord used to string violins and other instruments.

clue.text: Way traditions upset compound

parts.note: ST, short for street, is a way

indicators.note: in a down clue upset means turned upside down, so the word is read bottom to top

parts.note: lore is a body of traditions

explanation.surface: A way of life's traditions are overturned by some compound.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'upset' means flipped upright to inverted, so the traditions word is read upwards; 'Way' as a street abbreviation is easy to overlook.
explanation.definitionFit: A sterol is a chemical compound, a steroid alcohol such as cholesterol.

clue.text: Tyneside vicar backing humanist? Not again, not at any time!

definitions.text: Not again, not at any time

parts.note: Tyneside is in the North East of England, abbreviated NE

indicators.note: backing means going backwards, so the vicar's title is reversed

parts.note: REV, short for Reverend, is a vicar
Sir Thomas More was a celebrated Renaissance humanist

explanation.surface: A northern clergyman, supporting a secular thinker, vows never to do it again.
explanation.walkthrough: Tyneside is the area around Newcastle in north-east England; the humanist is Sir Thomas More, author of Utopia. 'backing' turns the vicar's title round.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means never again, the refrain of Poe's raven: at no time from now on.

clue.text: Flagrant lack of right-wingers mostly out to replace English

parts.note: no can mean a lack of, as in no money

indicators.note: the shortened word takes the place of the English abbreviation

parts.note: Tories are members of the British Conservative Party

indicators.note: mostly means all but the last letter of the word out

explanation.surface: A blatant absence of conservatives, mostly thrown out to make room for an Englishman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' looks like part of 'mostly out' meaning expelled, but 'mostly' just clips it to two letters, which 'to replace' substitutes for the English letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Flagrant and notorious both describe wrongdoing that is glaring and widely known.

clue.text: Spite of small number married after Victory in Europe

indicators.note: after places the number and married letter behind the Victory in Europe letters

parts.note: VE, as in VE Day, stands for Victory in Europe
NO is short for number

explanation.surface: A few wedded couples show malice after the wartime victory celebrations.
explanation.definitionFit: Venom figuratively means bitter malice or spite, from its literal sense of poison.

clue.text: Fulminate about awful night husband dispatched lemur?

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the ranting word goes round the rest

parts.note: to rail is to rant or fulminate

indicators.note: awful suggests something mangled, so the remaining letters are rearranged
dispatched means sent away, so the husband letter is removed

explanation.surface: Someone rages at a dreadful night after packing off a husband, perhaps over a lemur.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dispatched' removes the husband from the night before 'awful' scrambles what remains, giving INGT for 'about' to place within the ranting word.
explanation.definitionFit: The ring-tailed lemur of Madagascar is commonly called a ringtail for its banded tail.

clue.text: Seizer of chances left spades in one after work

indicators.note: after places the left and one pieces behind the work

parts.note: OP, short for opus, is a work
port is the left side of a ship

indicators.note: in puts the spades letter inside the word for one

parts.note: a unit is one
S is the abbreviation for spades in card games

explanation.surface: A card player grabbing chances leaves spades in a hand after work.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' puts S into UNIT, making UNIST.
explanation.definitionFit: An opportunist is someone who exploits chances as they arise, a grabber of openings.

clue.text: Reportedly see like some ocean-breeding creatures?

indicators.note: reportedly means as it is spoken, so the name of the see is said aloud

parts.note: a see is a bishop's seat; Ely is a cathedral city and diocese in Cambridgeshire

explanation.surface: A report about some sea creatures that breed far out in the ocean.
explanation.walkthrough: 'see' looks like a verb but is a bishop's diocese. Eels famously spawn in the Sargasso Sea, so the question mark flags a whimsical adjective.
explanation.definitionFit: Eely means resembling an eel, and eels migrate to the open ocean to breed.

clue.text: Threadbare Missouri girl, not quite eleven

parts.note: MO is the postal abbreviation for Missouri
Thea is a girl's name
a number just short of eleven is ten

explanation.surface: A shabbily dressed Missouri girl who is nearly eleven years old.
explanation.definitionFit: Moth-eaten fabric is worn and holed, so the word means shabby or worn out.

clue.text: Prickly type — certainly not a friend!

parts.note: no is a flat refusal
a pal is a friend

explanation.surface: A prickly person is emphatically no friend.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Prickly type' seems to describe a touchy person but is a cactus.
explanation.definitionFit: The nopal is the prickly pear cactus, a plant covered in spines.

clue.text: Propeller of vessel absent managers tie up outside back of hut

parts.note: someone out is absent
a board of directors manages a company

indicators.note: outside means the mooring word goes round the hut's letter

parts.note: to moor a boat is to tie it up

indicators.note: back of means the final letter of the word hut

explanation.surface: Missing directors tie their boat up behind a hut.
explanation.walkthrough: 'outside' puts MOOR round T, the back of 'hut', giving MOTOR.
explanation.definitionFit: An outboard motor is a detachable engine clamped to a boat's stern that drives it along.

clue.text: Extreme youth — time lad initially wears stranger headgear

indicators.note: the lad's letter wears the stranger word, so it goes inside it

parts.note: odder means stranger

indicators.note: initially picks the first letter of the word lad

parts.note: a hood is headgear

explanation.surface: A boy at an early age puts on some odd headgear.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wears' puts L, the first letter of 'lad', inside ODDER, giving ODDLER.
explanation.definitionFit: The stage of being a toddler is very early childhood, youth at its most extreme.

clue.text: Sensitivity is inclined to restrict some high-flyers

indicators.note: to restrict is to hem in, so the inclined word encloses the bird

parts.note: tends means is inclined, as in tends to agree
ernes are sea eagles, some of the high-flying birds

explanation.surface: Delicacy tends to hold back some ambitious achievers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'high-flyers' suggests ambitious people but means birds.
explanation.definitionFit: Tenderness can mean soreness to touch or emotional delicacy, both kinds of sensitivity.

clue.text: Naked belligerence ultimately shown by retired debt-collector

indicators.note: shown by places the letter next to the reversed collector
retired means withdrawn or going back, so the collector's word is reversed

parts.note: a dun is someone who demands payment of debts

indicators.note: ultimately picks the last letter of the word belligerence

explanation.surface: A retired bailiff finally shows aggression, and with no clothes on.
explanation.walkthrough: 'retired' turns DUN into NUD.
explanation.definitionFit: Nude and naked are direct synonyms for unclothed.

clue.text: Concern distributing most of dues after petition

indicators.note: after places the rearranged letters behind the petition word

parts.note: to solicit is to petition or ask for

indicators.note: distributing spreads letters about, so the shortened word is rearranged
most of means the word dues loses its last letter

explanation.surface: Worry about handing out most of the fees after a formal appeal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'most of' trims DUES to DUE; 'distributing' rearranges it to UDE.
explanation.definitionFit: Solicitude is anxious care for someone, a caring concern.

clue.text: Trendy style of art with strange unseemliness?

parts.note: in means fashionable or trendy
Art Deco is a decorative style, deco for short
rum is British slang for odd or strange

explanation.surface: A fashionable art style paired with something bizarre seems improper.
explanation.definitionFit: Indecorum is improper behaviour, a lack of decorum or propriety.

clue.text: She may drunkenly set about a large dog

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the rearranged letters go round the rest
drunkenly suggests staggering, so the letters of she may are rearranged

explanation.surface: A tipsy woman might set upon a big dog.
explanation.walkthrough: 'drunkenly' rearranges SHEMAY to SEYHAM, which 'about' wraps round A and L. 'set' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: The Sealyham is a small white Welsh terrier breed, so it is one kind of dog.

clue.text: Sea cook's fish? Fish or beef

parts.note: Long John Silver, the ship's cook in Treasure Island; with the apostrophe-s attached
the ide is a freshwater fish

explanation.surface: A ship's cook offers his fish, or perhaps beef.
explanation.walkthrough: SILVERSIDE is a British cut of beef from the hindquarter, and also a small silvery fish.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names both a small silver-striped fish and a cut of beef from the outer thigh.

clue.text: Pie, for example, that may be served inside

definitions.meaning: pie is an old name for the magpie, an example of a feathered creature
in slang, a prison sentence is served inside jail; doing time is called doing this

explanation.surface: A pie, and what may be served inside one.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pie' and 'served' suggest food, but one sense is the magpie and the other is British slang for a prison term.
explanation.definitionFit: A magpie is a bird; bird is also British rhyming slang (birdlime, time) for a prison sentence.

clue.text: Administrative area identified by capital H?

parts.note: Paris is the capital of France

explanation.surface: A district marked on a map by a capital letter H.
explanation.walkthrough: 'capital H' reads as an uppercase letter, but it is a capital city followed by H.
explanation.definitionFit: A parish is a local unit of church or civil government, a small administrative district.

clue.text: Fairground attraction — vessel on big wave

indicators.note: in an across clue, on means placed after, so the vessel follows the wave

parts.note: a roller is a long heavy sea wave
a coaster is a ship that trades along the coast

explanation.surface: A ship riding a huge wave is as thrilling as a fairground ride.
explanation.definitionFit: A rollercoaster is a fairground ride of steep rises and plunges on rails.

clue.text: Set of moral principles, and so on, covering Hawaii

indicators.note: covering means enclosing, so the et cetera letters go round the state's

parts.note: etc is short for et cetera, and so on
HI is the postal abbreviation for Hawaii

explanation.surface: Moral codes and the like spread over to Hawaii.
explanation.definitionFit: An ethic is a system of moral values guiding conduct.

clue.text: Wide boy's odds on girl getting rise

parts.note: SP, starting price, gives a horse's betting odds

indicators.note: in a down clue, getting a rise means going upwards, so the name is read bottom to top

parts.note: Vi is a girl's name, short for Violet

explanation.surface: A flashy dealer bets on his girlfriend getting a pay rise.
explanation.walkthrough: A spiv or wide boy is British slang for a flashy petty crook dealing in black-market goods. 'getting rise' turns VI to IV.
explanation.definitionFit: Wide boy and spiv are both British slang for a sharp, flashy small-time swindler.

clue.text: Nip back to lock up commander's dog

indicators.note: to lock up is to enclose, so the reversed word surrounds the commander
back means the word is read in reverse

parts.note: to nip somewhere is to hop there briefly
OC stands for Officer Commanding, a commander

explanation.surface: Pop back to shut away the commander's dog.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Nip' looks like a bite from the dog but means a quick trip; 'back' gives POH, which 'to lock up' wraps round the commander.
explanation.definitionFit: Pooch is informal slang for a dog.

clue.text: A woman's journal exhibited at first outside Italian museum?

parts.note: her means belonging to a woman

indicators.note: outside means those letters go round the Italian abbreviation

parts.note: a mag, short for magazine, is a journal

indicators.note: at first picks the opening letter of the word exhibited

explanation.surface: A woman's magazine first displayed in an Italian gallery.
explanation.walkthrough: The museum is the Hermitage in St Petersburg, hence the question mark for an example; 'outside' puts the journal and the first of 'exhibited' around the Italian.
explanation.definitionFit: The State Hermitage in St Petersburg is one of the world's great art museums.

clue.text: Single male trapped under a train?

indicators.note: trapped means held inside, so the single letter is enclosed
in a down clue, under means the male letter sits below the a

parts.note: I, the Roman numeral one, is single

explanation.surface: A lone man pinned beneath a railway train.
explanation.walkthrough: 'train' looks like a railway train but is the verb, to point a weapon.
explanation.definitionFit: To train a gun on something is to point it there, the same as taking aim.

clue.text: Organised medevac with little hesitation, producing handbook

indicators.note: organised means put into order, so the letters of medevac are rearranged

parts.note: um is a short sound of hesitation

explanation.surface: A medical evacuation arranged with barely a pause, following the manual.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Organised' rearranges MEDEVAC to VADEMEC.
explanation.definitionFit: A vade mecum, Latin for go with me, is a pocket reference book or manual.

clue.text: Soil constituent reeks, overwhelming university

indicators.note: overwhelming means engulfing, so the smelling word surrounds the university letter

parts.note: in British slang, hums means smells or reeks

explanation.surface: A smelly soil ingredient swamps a university.
explanation.definitionFit: Humus is the dark organic matter in soil formed from decayed plants.
